tasks.short: Answer site managers and department heads on budget rules, cost codes, capex approval and spending limits.

today.trigger: A question by mail or Teams from a site manager, HR or operations about a cost, budget or approval rule.
steps: Read the question and find the cost centre or invoice in AFAS
Look up the relevant policy on SharePoint or recall it
Check budget remaining in Power BI or an Excel export
Write the answer or call the person
Explain the same rule again at the next site
drudgery: Repeating the same answers on cost codes and approval limits
Hunting for the current version of a policy
today.time_sinks: Repeat questions from three sites and finding the current policy and budget figures before replying.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the answer from the SharePoint policy set and the AFAS budget figure, with the policy paragraph cited; the controller checks and sends. Lookup steps disappear, review takes a minute or two per question.
lenses.autonomous: A question in a shared Finance Teams channel starts a draft that cites policy and budget; routine answers on cost codes go out after the controller approves, anything about exceptions or approval limits stays with the controller.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for the 30 or so shift leaders and site managers in Tilburg and Venlo, who now rarely ask: a policy helpdesk in Teams with answers in Dutch. Demand would grow if answers were instant, which also means fewer miscoded invoices for the bookkeepers.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses explaining cost code 4410 for the tenth time; the controller wants more time on actual budget conversations with site managers.
lenses.options: Little value in several drafts; one cited answer is the right output.
lenses.altitude: The controller's week shifts from answering questions to curating the policy set and reviewing which questions recur, then changing rules or forms that cause them. Slightly more expert: the job becomes policy design.
reach: Bookkeeper: first-line coding questions from budget holders, by learning the AP coding rules in AFAS
FP&A Analyst: budget-remaining queries, by learning the Power BI budget model

tasks.human_edge: Knowing when a question is really a request for an exception, and saying no to a site manager in a way that keeps the relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns a free-text question plus retrieved policy text into a cited draft answer inside a fixed approve-and-send flow.

in_practice.trigger: New message in the Finance questions channel in Teams.
steps: Retrieve matching policy paragraphs from SharePoint and the cost centre budget from the nightly AFAS extract
Draft a Dutch answer citing the paragraph and figure
Controller approves, edits or takes over
Log question and answer to a FAQ list for policy review
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves every answer before it is sent; exceptions and approval-limit questions are never drafted as yes.
data_needed: Current policy documents with version dates
in_practice.logs_to: SharePoint list of questions, drafts, final answers and approver

evidence.claim: Retrieval-based answering over internal policy documents is mature in Microsoft 365 Copilot and similar tools.
Lab work shows models do well on structured close tasks but client communication and tacit context were not measured.

risks: Outdated policy versions on SharePoint produce confident wrong answers
Answers read as approvals for spending that was not approved
Budget figures one day stale from the nightly refresh
research_questions: How many policy questions does the controller get per month, and what share are repeats?
Is the SharePoint policy set current and complete enough to answer from?
Would site managers use a Teams channel rather than calling the controller directly?

tasks.short: Dig into site, customer and cost figures to find where margin leaks and what to improve.

today.trigger: Month close, a budget review, or a question from the Finance Director about a site or customer.
steps: Export ledger and cost centre data from AFAS or Power BI to Excel
Pull agency hours and invoices for flex labour
Build pivots by site, customer and cost type
Look for variances and trends
Write findings for the Finance Director or management team
drudgery: Re-building the same pivots each month
Matching agency invoices to hours and cost centres by hand
today.time_sinks: Data preparation and joining AFAS, agency and HR data takes most of the time; analysis gets what is left.

lenses.faster: Standard joins and variance tables run as fixed queries on the AFAS extract; a model drafts flux commentary and suggests where to look. The controller spends time on the two or three items that matter.
lenses.autonomous: After the nightly refresh on close day plus three, the variance pack and draft commentary are produced; the controller reviews before anything goes to management.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: margin per customer contract and per site reviewed monthly instead of at the annual tender, so loss-making warehouse contracts are repriced sooner. Demand from commercial would grow as it gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding pivots; the controller wants more time with site managers working out why Venlo flex costs jump in peak season.
lenses.options: Scenarios for flex versus permanent staffing levels per site, or pricing per customer, change the decision itself and are worth producing side by side.
lenses.altitude: The controller moves from producing analyses to choosing which questions management should ask, and gains a standing say in contract repricing and staffing mix. More expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly variance commentary, by learning the forecast model
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: flex labour cost dashboards, by learning the HR data in AFAS

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which variances are noise, what operations is not saying, and which finding management can act on.
tasks.pattern_why: The questions change each time and the controller leads; AI speeds data prep and drafting but does not pick the conclusions.

in_practice.trigger: Close day plus three, or an ad hoc question from the Finance Director.
steps: Fixed queries build variance tables by site, customer and cost type from the AFAS extract
Agency hours and invoices are matched to cost centres
Model drafts commentary and flags top variances
Controller investigates, rewrites and presents
in_practice.human_gate: Controller decides findings and recommendations before they reach management.
in_practice.logs_to: Monthly analysis pack on SharePoint with query versions

evidence.claim: Accountants using AI closed the month 7.5 days faster across 79 small and mid-sized firms.
The bottleneck on full close tasks is accounting judgement, not retrieval.

risks: Commentary sounds plausible but explains a variance wrongly
Agency data formats differ by agency and break the joins
Customer margin figures leak beyond management
research_questions: How many hours per month go to data prep versus analysis today?
Can agency hours be extracted in a stable format from all three portals?
Would commercial actually reprice contracts on monthly margin data?

tasks.short: Prepare for and run the year-end audit and internal checks; deliver the auditor's request list.

today.trigger: Interim and year-end audit by the external accountant, or an internal control check.
steps: Receive the auditor's request list (PBC list)
Pull samples, invoices, contracts and reconciliations from AFAS and SharePoint
Chase colleagues for missing evidence
Answer auditor questions and agree adjustments
Track open points in Excel
drudgery: Collecting documents for samples one by one
Chasing the same evidence each year
today.time_sinks: Finding and packaging evidence for sampled transactions and tracking open points.

lenses.faster: For each PBC item an evidence pack is assembled from AFAS documents and SharePoint and checked against the request; the controller reviews and releases. Collection time drops, auditor conversations stay.
lenses.autonomous: Receipt of the PBC list starts automatic collection and a status tracker; the controller approves each pack before it goes to the auditor.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: quarterly internal control tests on payments, IBAN changes and journal entries instead of only at year end, which should cut audit adjustments. Demand grows as tests get cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses copying PDFs into folders; the controller wants more time fixing the control weaknesses the audit finds.
lenses.options: Little use for multiple drafts; the evidence is what it is.
lenses.altitude: The controller runs the audit as a managed queue and owns the internal test calendar, with more say over which controls the auditor can rely on. More expert.
reach: Accountant: reconciliation evidence preparation, by learning the tie-out queries
Bookkeeper: invoice sample retrieval, by learning the AFAS document links

tasks.human_edge: Negotiating with the auditor on findings and adjustments, judging materiality, and knowing the story behind odd transactions.
tasks.pattern_why: Requests vary each year and the controller leads the audit; AI assembles and checks evidence under direction.

in_practice.trigger: PBC list received from the external auditor or a scheduled internal test date.
steps: Parse the PBC list into a tracker
Pull documents and ledger detail for each item from AFAS and SharePoint
Run fixed checks: totals tie, documents present, approvals recorded
Controller reviews each pack and sends to the auditor
in_practice.human_gate: Controller releases every pack and agrees every adjustment.
in_practice.logs_to: Audit tracker on SharePoint with pack versions and release dates

evidence.claim: Estimates the auditor cannot rebuild because prompts and outputs sit in personal accounts are a known failure.
Trintech's accruals agent keeps a 'Retain for Audit' trail after review and approval.

risks: Wrong document attached to a sample
Auditor does not accept AI-assembled evidence without a clear trail
Personal data in HR-related samples shared too widely (AVG)
research_questions: How many PBC items are there and how many hours go to collecting them?
Will the external auditor accept packs produced this way, and what trail do they need?
Are AFAS documents linked to entries consistently enough to retrieve automatically?

tasks.short: Write and update control rules for budgets, payments, credit and bookkeeping, including approval limits.

today.trigger: Audit finding, new risk (fraud attempt, IBAN change scam), new system, or annual review.
steps: Review the current procedure and the finding
Look at practice in AFAS workflows
Draft the new policy text in Word
Discuss with Finance Director and affected teams
Publish on SharePoint and adjust AFAS workflows
drudgery: Keeping SharePoint text and AFAS workflow settings in line
today.time_sinks: Drafting and redrafting text, and checking that the written rule matches how AFAS is configured.

lenses.faster: A model drafts the procedure from the finding, existing policy and a reference framework, and lists where AFAS settings differ from the text; the controller decides the rules and edits. Drafting time roughly halves.
lenses.autonomous: An audit finding or new risk opens a draft; nothing is published without the controller and Finance Director signing off.
lenses.ambitious: A new service for budget holders: one-page plain-Dutch control cards per role (site manager, buyer, HR) so rules are actually known on the floor; also a company rule on AI use in finance, which does not exist yet.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses formatting procedure documents; the controller wants more time testing whether controls work in practice.
lenses.options: Two or three versions of an approval matrix (tighter versus looser limits) change the decision on workload versus risk and are worth comparing.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the control framework as rules that are also enforced in AFAS, sets thresholds and decides where the model may draft. More expert.
reach: Accountant: procedure documentation, by learning the control framework
HR Director: expense and travel rules that touch employees, by learning works council consent rules

tasks.human_edge: Weighing risk against workload for 1,200 people, and getting budget holders and the works council to accept the rules.
tasks.pattern_why: One model call turns findings and existing text into a draft procedure and a gap list; the decision and approval flow are fixed.

in_practice.trigger: Audit finding logged, or annual policy review date.
steps: Collect the finding, current policy and AFAS workflow settings
Model drafts revised text and a list of gaps to AFAS configuration
Controller decides rules and thresholds
Finance Director approves; works council consulted where rules affect employees
Publish and update AFAS workflows
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and Finance Director approve before publication.
in_practice.logs_to: Policy register on SharePoint with versions and approvers

evidence.claim: Tax estimates and cash allocation need mandatory human review and timestamped logs, which a control policy should state.
Shadow AI use in accounting creates unrebuildable estimates, a gap a policy must close.

risks: Generic text that does not match how Noordhaven works
Rules that affect employees adopted without works council involvement (WOR art. 27)
Text and AFAS settings drift apart again
research_questions: Which policies are older than two years or contradicted by AFAS settings?
Which control rules require works council consent?
Does the auditor's management letter repeat the same findings year on year?

tasks.short: Prepare the year-end file for the tax adviser: corporate tax, VAT checks, fiscal reconciliation and KVK filing.

today.trigger: Year end and the deadlines for corporate income tax (Vpb), VAT and the KVK filing.
steps: Export the trial balance and fixed asset register from AFAS
Build the commercial-to-fiscal reconciliation in Excel
Reconcile VAT returns to the ledger
Answer the tax adviser's questions
Arrange the KVK filing via SBR outside AFAS
drudgery: Rebuilding the fiscal reconciliation workbook each year
Answering repeat questions from the tax adviser
today.time_sinks: Assembling and tying out the fiscal file and the back-and-forth with the adviser.

lenses.faster: Fixed queries build the trial balance, fiscal adjustments and VAT reconciliation; a model drafts the explanatory notes and pre-answers last year's adviser questions. The controller reviews and signs off.
lenses.autonomous: Once the year is closed, the tax file is built and tied out; it only goes to the adviser after the controller approves.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made more often: a quarterly VAT and fiscal check instead of a year-end one, so errors are found before filing. Moderate growth in demand if cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding the workbook; the controller wants time on the judgement calls, such as which costs are not deductible.
lenses.options: Little use for several drafts; the return is a single answer.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the fiscal mapping and the tie-out, and works with the adviser on judgement items only. Slightly more expert.
reach: Accountant: VAT reconciliation, by learning the VAT codes in AFAS
Finance Director: KVK filing preparation, by learning SBR requirements

tasks.human_edge: Judging grey-area items, owning the numbers towards the Belastingdienst, and handling the adviser relationship.
tasks.pattern_why: Numbers come from fixed queries with a tie-out; one model call drafts notes and answers inside that fixed flow.

in_practice.trigger: Year-end close marked complete in AFAS.
steps: Extract trial balance, fixed assets and VAT data
Apply the fiscal mapping and tie out to the ledger
Model drafts notes and answers to last year's questions
Controller reviews and sends to the tax adviser
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves the file; nothing goes to the adviser or the Belastingdienst until the tie-out is zero.
in_practice.logs_to: Tax file folder on SharePoint with query versions and approval

evidence.claim: Large companies file accounts with KVK via SBR from FY2025 and AFAS cannot do this for them.
Tax estimates need mandatory human review and approval with timestamped logs.
Benchmarks are US GAAP; Dutch fiscal rules and VAT returns are untested.

risks: Fiscal mapping errors carried forward silently
Model notes misstate Dutch tax treatment
Confidential tax data shared outside approved tools
research_questions: How many hours do the fiscal file and adviser questions take each year?
Is the commercial-to-fiscal mapping stable enough to fix as rules?
Will the tax adviser accept a standardised file and reduce their own fee?

tasks.short: Work out tax options with the adviser, such as investment allowances for electric trucks or warehouse solar.

today.trigger: Planned investments, a group structure change, or the adviser's year-end proposals.
steps: Collect planned capex and contracts
Check schemes (KIA, EIA, MIA/Vamil) and deadlines
Model effects in Excel
Discuss with tax adviser and Finance Director
Decide and file applications on time
today.time_sinks: Matching planned investments to scheme lists and keeping track of application deadlines.

lenses.faster: A model screens the capex list against current scheme lists and drafts scenario tables; the controller and adviser judge. Screening and spreadsheet time shrink.
lenses.autonomous: Every new capex request in AFAS is checked against the energy and environment lists and the controller is alerted of possible allowances and the three-month notification deadline.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: every capex request checked for tax allowances at the moment of ordering, not at year end when deadlines have passed. Demand grows as investments in electric fleet rise.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses scanning scheme lists; the controller wants more time on the investment choices themselves.
lenses.options: Scenarios (buy versus lease, timing across years, which allowance to claim) change the decision and are worth laying side by side.
lenses.altitude: The controller becomes the gate on tax effects of every investment rather than a year-end reviewer, with a say in capex timing. More expert.
reach: FP&A Analyst: capex scenario modelling, by learning the allowance rules
Accountant: application paperwork, by learning RVO procedures

tasks.human_edge: Judging tax risk and substance, and agreeing positions with the adviser and the Finance Director.
tasks.pattern_why: Tax planning needs judgement on each case; AI screens and models while the controller leads.

in_practice.trigger: New capex request or purchase order above a threshold in AFAS.
steps: Fetch the request and description
Model screens against the current scheme lists and drafts the possible allowance
Controller confirms with adviser
Track the notification deadline
in_practice.human_gate: Controller and tax adviser decide every claim.

evidence.claim: Models still fail on tasks that need accounting judgement; 58% of close tasks are never fully solved.
Dutch investment allowances such as EIA and MIA/Vamil have notification deadlines that a screen can track.

risks: Scheme lists change yearly and the model uses old lists
Missed deadline still possible if purchase descriptions are vague
Over-reliance on model tax views without adviser check
research_questions: How many allowances were missed in the last three years because of late notification?
How many capex requests per year could qualify?
Does the tax adviser already offer such screening?

tasks.short: Set depreciation periods for trucks, forklifts and racking, and advise on buy, lease or dispose.

today.trigger: New asset purchase, lease renewal, fleet replacement plan, or an asset sold or scrapped.
steps: Check asset class and useful life in the AFAS fixed asset register
Gather quotes and lease offers
Build a buy versus lease comparison in Excel
Write a memo for the Finance Director or management
Book the asset or disposal in AFAS
drudgery: Rebuilding the buy versus lease spreadsheet for each case
today.time_sinks: Collecting offers and building the comparison each time.

lenses.faster: A fixed asset class table and a standard buy, lease and dispose model compute the figures from the offer inputs; the controller checks assumptions and writes the advice. Comparison time drops to under an hour.
lenses.autonomous: A new asset request or lease renewal fills the model with offer data; the controller approves the classification and the advice.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the fleet and warehouse managers: a replacement plan per site for forklifts and trucks with a lease-or-buy view for each, reviewed yearly. Demand would grow as electrification brings many decisions.
lenses.joy: Nobody misses rebuilding NPV sheets; the controller wants more time negotiating with lessors and fleet managers.
lenses.options: Buy, lease and keep-longer scenarios side by side change the decision and should be shown together.
lenses.altitude: The controller owns the asset policy and the standard model, and joins fleet decisions early rather than booking them after. More expert.
reach: Accountant: fixed asset register upkeep, by learning the asset class table
FP&A Analyst: capex plan, by learning the replacement model

tasks.human_edge: Judging real useful life given shift intensity per site, and reading lease contract terms and residual value risk.
tasks.pattern_why: Depreciation rules and an NPV comparison can be written down and built quickly; no model is needed to run them.

in_practice.trigger: Asset request, lease renewal or disposal entered in AFAS.
steps: Classify the asset against the asset class table
Run buy, lease and keep scenarios with the standard model
Controller checks assumptions and writes the advice
Book in AFAS after approval
in_practice.human_gate: Controller approves classification and advice; Finance Director signs above the capex threshold.
systems: Excel or a small Python tool
data_needed: Asset class and useful life table
in_practice.logs_to: Fixed asset register in AFAS and decision memos on SharePoint

evidence.claim: Lease accounting under Dutch GAAP (RJ 292) differs from IFRS 16, which affects the comparison.
Models solve simple close scenarios well in a lab, but judgement-heavy tasks remain unsolved.

risks: Wrong useful life for heavily used equipment on multiple shifts
Model assumptions treated as fixed truth
Lease terms not entered completely
research_questions: How many buy, lease or dispose decisions are there per year?
Do actual useful lives of forklifts and trucks match the register?
Can usage hours per asset be pulled from fleet systems?

role.altitude: From preparing analyses, files and answers by hand to designing the close and control system: the controller owns the accrual and policy handbook, tie-out queries, materiality and approval thresholds, the asset class table and the audit trail, and decides where a model may draft and where a person must approve.
reach: FP&A Analyst: monthly variance commentary and capex scenarios
Accountant: fixed asset register, VAT reconciliation and audit evidence packs
Bookkeeper: first-line coding questions from budget holders
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: flex labour cost analysis per site
role.ceiling_note: Limited by judgement work that stays human: auditor and tax adviser negotiation, materiality calls, Dutch GAAP and fiscal grey areas untested by US GAAP benchmarks, and works council involvement for rules that affect employees. Realistic saving is around 35% of the hours on these tasks, not more.
skills_to_grow: SQL and Power BI on the AFAS extract
Writing and testing prompts and evaluation sets for finance drafts
Control design that is enforced in AFAS workflows
AI governance basics: AVG, EU AI Act scope and audit trails
role.ambitious_version: Monthly margin per customer contract and site, quarterly control tests, and capex screened for tax allowances at ordering, so the Finance Director gets a trusted forecast and fewer audit adjustments, with the controller as designer of the system rather than preparer of its outputs.
